body.text: Is the Harem section included in the 2026 combined Topkapı ticket?

Yes. Under the 2026 [Presidency of National Palaces (Milli Saraylar)](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Bilet/BiletAl) fee structure, the standard 2,750 TL foreign-visitor combined ticket automatically includes the Main Palace, the Harem quarters, and Hagia Irene church. You no longer need to queue twice for a separate Harem add-on ticket inside the Second Courtyard.

This combined structure simplifies entry, though it catches travelers off guard if they still read pre-2024 guides quoting separate Harem surcharges. Standalone Harem-only or Hagia Irene-only tickets exist at 1,050 TL each per [2026 Topkapı pricing records](https://hotelperula.com/en/blog/topkapi-palace-guide/), yet skipping the Harem removes the palace's finest 16th- and 17th-century Iznik tilework, including the Queen Mother's apartments, the Twin Pavilions, and the Imperial Hall. Note that Topkapı Palace is managed by [Milli Saraylar](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/2/Topkapi-Sarayi) rather than the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, so verify pass eligibility before assuming a standard Ministry pass covers every section.
What order avoids bottlenecks at the Treasury and Sacred Relics?

Enter through the Gate of Salutation at 09:00 sharp and walk directly past the Second Courtyard into the Third Courtyard to visit the Imperial Treasury (Fatih Köşkü) and the Sacred Relics Chamber first. Tour groups spend their first 45 minutes lecturing in the Second Courtyard, leaving the tightest indoor rooms clear until 10:15.

Following its major structural restoration, the [Imperial Treasury in Fatih Köşkü](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Kurumsal/HaberDetay/55/Topkapi-Sarayinda-Buyuk-Acilis) houses the 86-carat Spoonmaker's Diamond and the emerald-studded Topkapı Dagger in narrow galleries where queues back up quickly by late morning. Next door, the reorganized Sacred Relics Department (Hırka-i Saadet Dairesi) displays roughly 300 relics and now allows visitors to step directly inside the domed Has Oda. After finishing both rooms and pausing on the Fourth Courtyard's Bosphorus terrace, double back to the Harem around 10:45, then finish with the spacious Palace Kitchens and Imperial Council Hall on your way out.

body.text: How many hours do you realistically need?

Plan 3 to 4 full hours inside Topkapı Palace if you include the Harem, Treasury, Sacred Relics, Fourth Courtyard pavilions, and Hagia Irene without sprinting. Visitors who budget under two hours usually end up skipping either the Harem or the porcelain and arms galleries due to walking distances and security queues.

Topkapı is not a single European-style palace building; it is an imperial campus of four sprawling courtyards, gardens, and low pavilions built over four centuries. Walking from the Imperial Gate to the Fourth Courtyard marble terrace and back covers nearly two kilometers on stone pavers. Modest attire (covered shoulders and knees) is strictly enforced inside the Sacred Relics Chamber, and photography is prohibited in both the Treasury and Sacred Relics rooms.

Topkapı Palace—including the Harem and Hagia Irene—is closed every Tuesday, per the official [Milli Saraylar visiting schedule](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/AnaSayfa/ZiyaretBilgileri). This trips up many travelers because Dolmabahçe Palace and most other National Palaces in Istanbul close on Mondays instead, making Monday an active day at Topkapı and Tuesday a quiet one.

Standard visiting hours run 09:00 to 17:00 (extended toward 17:30–18:00 during peak summer months, with last ticket sales closing an hour prior). Because Tuesday removes Topkapı from your Sultanahmet loop, pair Tuesday with the neighboring Istanbul Archaeological Museums, the Basilica Cistern, or Dolmabahçe Palace up the Bosphorus.

items: Confirm your visit does not fall on a Tuesday or the morning of a major religious holiday.
Wear supportive flat shoes for uneven courtyard cobbles and bring a light scarf or layer for the Sacred Relics Chamber.
Enter via the Sultanahmet or Gülhane T1 tram stop before 09:00.
Start at the Treasury and Sacred Relics before looping back to the Harem.
Keep your combined QR ticket accessible—staff scan it again at the Harem and Hagia Irene entrances.

faq.q: How much is the Topkapı Palace ticket in 2026?
faq.a: The official foreign-visitor combined ticket (Main Palace + Harem + Hagia Irene) is 2,750 TL at the gate or through [Milli Saraylar](https://muze.gen.tr/muze-detay/topkapi).

faq.q: Can I buy a ticket for the Main Palace without the Harem?
faq.a: For foreign visitors in 2026, Milli Saraylar sells the all-in combined ticket (2,750 TL) as the primary admission rather than a cheaper Palace-only option.

faq.q: Is Topkapı Palace open on Mondays?
faq.a: Yes. Topkapı Palace is open on Mondays from 09:00 and closes on Tuesdays—the exact opposite of Dolmabahçe Palace.

faq.q: Are audio guides included with the combined ticket?
faq.a: Audio guides are available at the entrance kiosk after security; carry a photo ID or check current rental terms at the counter before entering the Second Courtyard.

faq.q: Is there a dress code inside Topkapı Palace?
faq.a: Standard sightseeing attire is fine for the courtyards and Harem, but shoulders and knees must be covered to enter the Sacred Relics Chamber.

faq.q: Does Topkapı Palace offer night visits in 2026?
faq.a: Milli Saraylar has launched seasonal [evening openings at Topkapı Palace](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Kurumsal/HaberDetay/113/TOPKAPI-SARAYI-NDA-GECE-ZIYARETLERI-BASLADI) on select summer Saturdays with separate tickets; check the official website for active dates.
